Easier first install: one command installs everything, and the app tells you when Hermes Agent is missing or has no AI provider yet.

## Install

**One command** in PowerShell. It installs Hermes Agent too if it's missing, checks the installer against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and opens the app:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nexurlabs/hermes-bots/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

**Or by hand:** download **`Hermes-Bots-Setup-1.8.5.exe`** below and run it. It installs over 1.x and keeps your settings and chats. Check the download against **`SHA256SUMS.txt`** (PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\Hermes-Bots-Setup-1.8.5.exe`).

- **Not code-signed.** Windows SmartScreen will say "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info → Run anyway**.
- No auto-update: install a newer `Hermes-Bots-Setup-<version>.exe` over this one.
- **Needs Hermes Agent v0.22.3 or newer.** Not installed yet? See *Step 0* in the README, or just open the app: it shows the one-line install command.

## New

- **One-command install** for Windows (above). It asks for this PC or a VPS. A VPS gets the app only; add it under **Settings → Machines**.
- **"Hermes Agent isn't installed on this computer"** screen instead of `spawn hermes ENOENT`, with the install command for your system (copy button), a link to the install guide and **Retry**.
- **No AI provider yet?** A small notice says so and tells you to type `/login` in chat or run `hermes model` / `hermes setup` on the Hermes machine. The app doesn't ask for API keys; Hermes's own onboarding handles them.
- **Clearer SSH key errors:** picking a public key (`.pub`) says to choose the private key; a key file this Windows account can't read says so instead of "not found"; the permissions message says the owner must be your own account.

## Fixes

- **The first start after a Hermes update no longer fails with "Hermes took too long to start".** Hermes runs its setup on that start, which can take minutes. Connect now waits up to 30 minutes while it runs and says "Hermes is finishing an update". Clicking Connect again waits for the same start instead of launching a second one.
- Refused calls to the app's tool server now log which route they hit and why, never the token.

## Build and release

- Every release installer is now installed silently on a Windows runner and launched before it's published (smoke test), and the same check runs on pull requests.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached to each release. It's written after signing, so it matches the file you download.
- Releases can be signed by SignPath Foundation once the project's application is approved. Until then they're unsigned.
- CI installs from the frozen `bun.lock`. README now uses Bun commands.
- Demo data no longer contains personal paths.
